01 / The challenge

What the job asks of your van.

Roofing vans carry ladders, racks and materials that can hide large parts of the bodywork. A good layout keeps your name and number visible when everything is loaded, and stands up to the dirt and weather of site work. Whether you need roofing company van wraps, roofing pickup graphics or roofing contractor van livery, the layout has to work on your vehicle as it really is.

01

Ladders on the roof

Roof racks and ladder clamps cover the top of the sides. Key information has to sit lower.

02

Dusty, dirty work

Graphics need to stay readable when the van is covered in site dust.

03

Seen on site

Your van parked outside a job is your advert for the whole street.

02 / What to include

What your van must say.

  • Business name
  • Roofing services, e.g. flat roofs or repairs
  • Phone number on sides and rear
  • Insurance-backed guarantees, if offered

Not sure what to include? Our guide to what to put on a work van walks you through it.

06 / Design tips

Build the layout around the job.

01

Photograph the van fully loaded

Send photos with ladders and racks fitted so the layout avoids them.

02

Use solid colours

Large solid blocks stay visible even when dusty.

03

Keep services short

Flat roofing, slating and repairs read better than a long list.

Before you book

Good to know.

Will the graphics survive site work?

Yes. We use durable cast films with laminate that resist abrasion and cleaning.

Can you brand my pickup too?

Yes. We can adapt the same design to a pickup or tipper.

Should I mention guarantees?

If you offer an insurance-backed guarantee, it is worth a short line.
